body.text: Goals: Show where Wayne comes from & how the South was viewed. “How does young Wayne sound compared to older Wayne?” Teaches evolution.

Baby & Slim molding Wayne as a franchise player
Why “Tha Block Is Hot” mattered for a teenage rapper
Southern rap’s stigma in the late 90s → early 2000s

lessons.title: Tha Carter I & II — The Rap Technician Emerges

body.text: Emerges Goals: Show Wayne turning himself into a lyricist. Discussion: “What technical skills is Wayne showing here?” Flow? Breath control? Wordplay? Cadence switching?

body.label: Key points
items: Tha Carter I = new persona, new confidence
Tha Carter II = sharpened punchlines + grown-man cadence
Wayne out-rapping East Coast rappers on their own beats
Dedication to the craft, not just the image

body.text: Drought 3, S.Q. Series Goals: Teach the why behind Wayne’s dominance. Ask him (when older): “Why did Wayne call himself the best rapper alive? Do you hear it?”

Flooded the market to starve competition
Built a mythology around his pen
Taught rap fans to chase bars, not singles
